query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a secondary phase via precipitation of Co-rich nanoparticles in a single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy matrix can increase the coercive field by pinning domain walls and reducing magnetic domain size.
generation.intervention: Precipitation of Co-rich nanoparticles through aging at 500°C for 10 hours
generation.conditions: Aging temperature: 500°C, Aging time: 10 hours, Particle size: 5-10 nm
generation.mechanism: Domain wall pinning and reduction of magnetic domain size
generation.predicted_outcome: Increase in coercive field by 50% relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty in particle size distribution and aging temperature control

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled aging experiment with varying particle sizes and aging temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercive field does not increase by at least 30% relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi for particle sizes between 5-10 nm and aging temperatures between 450°C and 550°C, the hypothesis is falsified.
